documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Regional hospital - medicine service
Admitted 06/28/2024 via the emergency department. Discharged 07/03/2024.

Reason for admission: left foot ulcer, 3 weeks, not healing.

History: 69-year-old man with type 2 diabetes for about 18 years and diabetic neuropathy. The ulcer started as a blister from a new pair of shoes and has grown larger and deeper. No fever or chills. More redness lately and a bad smell from the wound. Also hypertension, chronic AF on warfarin, prior nasal BCC, pharyngeal pouch repair, right cataract surgery with endophthalmitis, normal coronary angiogram 12/2023.
Home meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, warfarin 5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, capsaicin cream.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Exam on arrival: afebrile. Left foot ulcer 3 cm across with a purulent base and surrounding erythema; no crepitus. Light touch diminished in both feet. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses weak on both sides.
Labs: WBC 14.0, hemoglobin A1c 9.2%, ESR 70 mm/hr, CRP 15 mg/dL. INR 2.4.
Imaging: foot X-ray with cortical erosion next to the ulcer. ABI 0.98 right, 0.96 left.

Diagnosis: diabetic foot infection with osteomyelitis, left foot.

Hospital course: Started on IV vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam. Podiatric surgery performed debridement of the ulcer and underlying bone with bone biopsy on 06/30 (warfarin held beforehand). Bone culture grew methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus; antibiotics narrowed to cefazolin. PICC placed 07/02. Blood sugars managed with correction insulin while inpatient; metformin resumed. Warfarin resumed 07/01.

Discharge medications: cefazolin 2 g IV every 8 hours via home infusion through 08/11/2024 (6 weeks); continue home medications unchanged.
Wound care: daily dressing per home nursing; offloading boot, no bare-foot walking.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week; infectious disease in 6 weeks; podiatry in 1 week. INR weekly while on cefazolin (may raise INR).

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Home since 7/3 after admission for left foot ulcer with osteomyelitis (MSSA on bone culture). Home infusion nurse running cefazolin every 8 hours through the PICC, dressing changes daily. Wearing the boot. No fever, eating well. Podiatry saw him last week, wound looks better per them.

Meds reconciled: cefazolin 2 g IV q8h to 8/11, plus his usual metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ, warfarin 5, atorvastatin, capsaicin. NKDA.

O: Vitals as charted, afebrile. PICC right arm clean, no redness. Left foot dressing clean and dry, not taken down (podiatry managing). Right foot intact.

A/P:
1. Diabetic foot infection with osteomyelitis - on 6 weeks of cefazolin, ID follow-up 8/12, podiatry weekly.
2. AF on warfarin - INR 2.9 on cefazolin. Weekly INR until antibiotics done; RN to call results.
3. T2DM - A1c 9.2 in hospital. Continue metformin.
4. HTN - controlled.
RTC after ID visit.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
INDICATION: Acute right lower quadrant pain, fever.
FINDINGS: The appendix is thickened and inflamed with a focal wall defect and an adjacent rim-enhancing fluid collection in the right lower quadrant, consistent with an appendiceal abscess. Surrounding fat stranding. No free intraperitoneal air. Liver, pancreas, spleen, adrenal glands and kidneys normal. No bowel obstruction. No adenopathy.

SPECIMEN: Appendix.
DIAGNOSIS: Acute suppurative appendicitis with perforation and periappendiceal abscess. No dysplasia or neoplasm identified.
reports.conclusion: Perforated acute appendicitis with abscess; no neoplasm.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital - general surgery
Admitted 12/25/2024 from the emergency department; discharged 12/28/2024.

Presentation: 70-year-old man with diabetes and a left foot infection treated earlier this year, with right lower quadrant abdominal pain that started abruptly about 6 hours before arrival. No nausea or vomiting, no change in bowel habits.
Medications: warfarin 5 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: T 38.1 C (100.6 F), BP 145/90, pulse 85 and irregularly irregular, RR 18. Tender in the right lower quadrant with rebound.
Labs: Hgb 13.2, WBC 14.0, INR 3.8, creatinine 1.1, BUN 21.
CT: appendiceal abscess.

Course: Surgery recommended urgent appendectomy because of the risk of rupture. To correct the INR before surgery he received vitamin K 10 mg IV and four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate; repeat INR 1.4. Laparoscopic appendectomy that evening with drainage of the periappendiceal abscess. Pathology: acute suppurative appendicitis with perforation and abscess, no neoplasm. IV piperacillin-tazobactam postoperatively. Diet advanced on day 1. Warfarin restarted 12/27 at 5 mg, no bridging. Afebrile and tolerating food at discharge.

Discharge medications: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily for 7 days; resume all home medications.
Follow-up: INR with primary care 12/31; surgery clinic in 2 weeks; primary care in 1-2 weeks.

orders.reason: Epigastric pain, weight loss, abnormal liver tests - urgent

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About two and a half months of a constant gnawing ache in the upper abdomen. Not clearly tied to meals. Appetite poor, eating maybe half of what he used to. Weight down from 86 kg in September to 79 today. No vomiting, no black stools. He hasn't noticed yellow skin or eyes.

O: Vitals as charted. Looks thinner in the face. Sclerae anicteric in office light. Abdomen soft, mild epigastric discomfort to deep palpation, no mass felt, no rebound. Irregular rhythm, controlled.

A/P: Epigastric pain with unintended weight loss, age 71, family history of pancreatic cancer in a paternal uncle - concerning. CMP, CBC, lipase today. Urgent GI referral placed. Will call with results today.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. Bilirubin 2.1, alk phos 265, AST 62, ALT 70 - new cholestatic pattern; lipase normal at 38; CBC unremarkable. Spoke with GI office, they will see him 12/29 and likely image first. Told him to go to the ED for yellowing with fever, vomiting or worse pain. He understands. Continue warfarin and other meds for now.

reports.text:
INDICATION: Jaundice, epigastric pain.
FINDINGS: Intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts are dilated. The gallbladder is distended without gallstones, sludge or wall thickening. A hypoechoic mass is present in the head of the pancreas. Liver normal in echotexture without focal lesion. Spleen normal size. Kidneys normal. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Biliary dilation without gallstones; hypoechoic pancreatic head mass.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology practice
Date of visit: 12/29/2025
Re: Eugene Connolly, 71 M

Urgent referral from primary care. Three months of constant gnawing epigastric pain, poor appetite and marked weight loss; over the past week he and others have noticed yellowing of his skin and eyes. Background: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, atrial fibrillation on warfarin, neuropathy, pharyngoesophageal diverticulum repaired 2022.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, warfarin 5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg. Allergies: none known.
Family: paternal uncle with pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

Exam: weight 77 kg. Cachectic. Skin and sclerae icteric. Abdomen: a distended, non-tender gallbladder is palpable; no other mass, no ascites.

Labs today: total bilirubin 5.2, direct 3.8, alkaline phosphatase 420, AST 85, ALT 90, CA 19-9 150.
Ultrasound today: dilated intra- and extrahepatic ducts, no stones, hypoechoic mass in the pancreatic head.

Impression: obstructive jaundice from a pancreatic head mass, highly concerning for malignancy.
Plan: pancreas-protocol CT next week, then EUS with fine-needle aspiration and ERCP with biliary stenting in one session. Warfarin to be held before EUS/ERCP; we will coordinate with his PCP.
